Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience and / or training.
Experience serving and supporting graduate students.

Under the general direction of the Graduate Program Manager and Advisor, the Graduate Advisor serves as the primary specialist for graduate degree programs in assigned departments. The incumbent is responsible and accountable for the overall development, oversight, and coordination of all programmatic activities and support services for graduate programs. While graduate advisors divide primary workloads along departmental lines, they collaborate closely to reflect the interdisciplinary nature of BE academic programs - frequently cross-advising students and providing coverage or backup for one another as needed.

With this wide scope of responsibility, the Graduate Advisor applies knowledge of policies and procedures pertinent to graduate education at UCSC generally and BE specifically to problem-solve while interacting directly with faculty and graduate students in BE programs. Ensuring consolidated and cooperative services for all graduate students, the incumbent is often required to move seamlessly between unique programs with separate requirements and distinct tracks of study.

BE faculty significantly rely on the Graduate Advisor to independently oversee support services, coordinate policy implementation and compliance, and accurately interpret and apply policies and procedures. The Graduate Advisor routinely advises faculty on issues requiring direct faculty involvement, ensures graduate student welfare, allocates resources, and guides the continued expansion of BE graduate programs in accordance with academic planning goals.
